source.description: Project fuzz entry calls libxml2 xmlReadMemory to parse the attacker-controlled XSLT stylesheet bytes into a document tree.

sink.description: Second free of a text node content pointer while freeing the stylesheet document tree.

root_cause.description: Stylesheet preprocessing skips descending into entity-like child nodes, leaving a malformed/unprocessed child ownership state that later allows the same text node content to be freed through both a temporary template tree and stylesheet document cleanup.

taint_source.description: The attacker-controlled XSLT bytes are parsed into an XML document tree.

tainted_value_origin.description: The XML parser materializes attacker-controlled stylesheet text content as a heap-owned text node buffer.

coarse_trace.summary: Attacker-controlled XSLT bytes are parsed with xmlReadMemory.
Stylesheet preprocessing fails to recurse into entity-like child nodes before transformation.
Transformation evaluates an xsl:message template string.
The temporary insert node is freed, releasing the shared text content.
Freeing the stylesheet document frees the same text content again.

fine_trace.note: Project parser source: the PoC bytes are parsed as an XSLT stylesheet document.

grounding.evidence: No sanitizer or patch artifact directly grounded this step.

fine_trace.note: ASan allocation context: attacker-controlled text content is copied into an XML text node.

grounding.evidence: No sanitizer or patch artifact directly grounded this step.

fine_trace.note: The parsed stylesheet document is handed to libxslt stylesheet preprocessing.

grounding.evidence: No sanitizer or patch artifact directly grounded this step.

fine_trace.note: Root cause: the vulnerable traversal skips entity-like children instead of always descending, leaving child node ownership/processing inconsistent. The patch replaces this conditional skip with unconditional descent into cur->children.

grounding.evidence: Step is on a changed patch line or a patch hunk line with a patch-groundable role.

fine_trace.code: result = xsltApplyStylesheetUser(sheet, doc, NULL, NULL, NULL, ctxt);
fine_trace.note: The preprocessed stylesheet is executed; the crashing input reaches xsl:message evaluation.

grounding.evidence: Step is in the same sanitizer crash-stack function within a small source-line drift window.

fine_trace.note: The message instruction evaluates a template string from the affected stylesheet subtree.

grounding.evidence: No sanitizer or patch artifact directly grounded this step.

fine_trace.note: First free: freeing the temporary insert tree releases the affected text node content; ASan free_stack reaches this path.
After transformation, stylesheet cleanup frees the stylesheet XML document.

grounding.evidence: Step file/line appears in sanitizer crash_stack.

fine_trace.note: Document cleanup walks the stylesheet document children.

grounding.evidence: Step file/line appears in sanitizer crash_stack.

fine_trace.note: ASan crash location: the same text content is freed again while freeing the stylesheet document tree.

grounding.evidence: Step file/line appears in sanitizer crash_stack.

root_cause_analysis.summary: The PoC is parsed as an XSLT stylesheet. The XML parser allocates text node content from attacker-controlled input. During stylesheet preprocessing, xsltParseStylesheetProcess() skips descending into entity-like child nodes, so the affected child subtree is not normalized in the same way as ordinary children. Later, xsl:message evaluation builds/frees a temporary insert tree, freeing the text node content once. Finally, xsltFreeStylesheet() frees the stylesheet document, and xmlFreeNodeList() frees the same content again.
root_cause_analysis.why_patch_works: The patch removes the entity-type guard and always descends into cur->children when children exist, so those child nodes are processed consistently before transformation. That prevents the malformed ownership state that allowed the same text node content to be released by both temporary-template cleanup and stylesheet document cleanup.
